1. Using a feeler gauge, measure the distance between the bevel dummy pinion plane and the dummy ring gear.

1. The stamp (A) corresponds to the identification number for the differential ring gear; the same number is also on the bevel pinion shaft because the two components must be matched. If one of the two components has to be replaced then the other one with the same number also has to be replaced. The stamp (B) on the pinion shaft indicates the VP value.

After the measurement has been taken, determine the size of the scraper ring for the bevel pinion using the following formula.

S = [X + (± VP)] ± 0,04

S = thickness of scraper ring (mm)

X = value measured using feeler gauge (mm)

VP = value shown on pinion

0.04 = tolerance (mm)

The value VP can be either positive or negative.The spacers available vary from a minimum of 0.51 mm to a maximum of 1.40 mm in increments of 0.05 mm.

Example of numerical calculation with positive VP.

Let us suppose that the following figures have been obtained:

X = 1.15 mm (feeler gauge reading)

VP = + 2 = 0,02 mm

S = (1,15 + 0,02) ± 0,04 mm = 1,13 ÷ 1,21

Example of numerical calculation with negative VP.

Let us suppose that the following figures have been obtained:

X = 1.15 mm (feeler gauge reading)

VP = -2 = -0.02 mm

S = (1,15 -0.02) ± 0,04 mm = 1.09 ÷ 1.17
